title: The legend of Tataka
introduction: While crossing over the River Ganga, sage Vishvamitra sails them through its confluence with River Sarayu, which flows at their capital Ayodhya. The sage leads them to a deadly forest on the other bank of River Ganga and narrates about the ambushing nature of demoness Tataka, preparing him to kill her.
closing: The epithets used in epic may be on the increase from now, and they may not be construed as redundant foot fillers. All have implicit meanings and they can be understood with the help of commentaries. As this work cannot include voluminous commentaries, many of the meanings of epithets as said by commentators are not incorporated. This bypassing will not effect the ordinary narration. For e.g., the meaning to the words munipungava, naraśārdūlawill be 'the eminent saint' 'tigerly man'. And trying to obtain a squeezed meaning from them would be futile, without resorting to some commentary. So also, there are words like indra, candra, simha, śārdūla, nāga, vṛṣabha, pungavawhich when suffixed to vocatives will mean 'best, choicest, excellent' etc., as per simha-śārdūla-nāgādyāḥ pumsi śreṣṭārthagocarāḥ. But commentators have explained why that character is 'best or excellent, or a lion' at that juncture. For e.g., dharmātmāthe apparently usual epithet in Ramayana has many meanings like – 1] one whose life is dharma; 2] one whose body is dharma incarnate; 3] one whose soul is filled with dharma; 4] one whose entity itself is dharma – so on, basing on the thesaurus of ātmathat say as: ātmā yatna-dhṛti-svānta-svabhāva-paramātmāsu jīva-buddhi- śarīreṣu..

So also, more than often Seetha will be referred as Vaidehi or Maithili in Aranya Kanda. Some details about it are incorporated in that book. Wherever possible those niceties will be included subject to availability of commentaries, which commentaries have already became 'the flowers in the sky.'

Hence, without trying to squeeze meaningless meanings, and leaving this aspect to pundits and researchers, and as this work cannot be stuffed with those intricacies, henceforth the meanings of epithets are said simply, and at times ignored also. This may please be kept in view while reading.
इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः ||
Thus, this is the 24th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रभाते विमले कृताह्निकमरिन्दमौ |
विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य नद्यास्तीरमुपागतौ
verses.iast:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale kṛta āhnikam arindamau |
viśvāmitram puraskṛtya nadyāḥ tīram upāgatau
verses.translation: Then, in the fresh of the morning those enemy destroyers, Rama and Lakshmana, arrived at the riverbank of Ganga keeping sage Vishvamitra ahead of them, which sage has just completed his ritualistic chores of dawn.

glosses.meaning: one who [just now] performed, morning ritual tasks, Vishvamitra

verses.devanagari:
ते च सर्वे महात्मानो मुनयः संश्रितव्रताः |
उपस्थाप्य शुभां नावं विश्वामित्रमथाब्रुवन्
verses.iast:
te ca sarve mahātmāno munayaḥ saṃśrita vratāḥ |
upasthāpya śubhām nāvam viśvāmitram atha abruvan
verses.translation: All those sages of Kaama's hermitage that are the great souls and scrupulous ones in their vows, have positioned an auspicious ferryboat within the reach in the river, and then they said to sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: great souls, scrupulous ones, in their vows
those, also, all, sages [of that hermitage]
to then, to Vishvamitra, they said.

verses.devanagari:
आरोहतु भवान्नावं राजपुत्रपुरस्कृतः |
अरिष्टं गच्छ पन्थानं मा भूत्कालविपर्ययः
verses.iast:
ārohatu bhavān nāvam rājaputra puraskṛtaḥ |
ariṣṭam gaccha panthānam mā bhūt kāla viparyayaḥ
verses.translation: "You may board the boat keeping the princes ahead of you, and we wish you to proceed on a prosperous route without the shift of time." So said the sages.

glosses.meaning: you, king's, sons, keeping ahead of you
let not be there - without time-shift.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रस्तथेत्युक्त्वा तानृषीन्प्रतिपूज्य च |
ततार सहितस्ताभ्यां सरितं सागरंगमाम्
verses.iast:
viśvāmitraḥ tathā iti uktvā tān ṛṣīn pratipūjya ca |
tatāra sahitaḥ tābhyām saritam sāgaram gamām
verses.translation: Sage Vishvamitra on saying 'it must be so,' to those sages and revering them in his turn, cruised the river that itself is cruising towards ocean, along with both the princes.

glosses.meaning: 'it must be so', thus, on saying
them, the sages, in turn, revering

verses.devanagari:
तत्र शुश्राव वै शब्दं तोयसंरम्भवर्धितम् |
मध्यमागम्य तोयस्य तस्य शब्दस्य निश्चयम्
ज्ञातुकामो महातेजा सह रामः कनीयसा |
verses.iast:
tatra śuśrāva vai śabdam toya saṃrambha vardhitam |
madhyam āgaṃya toyasya tasya śabdasya niścayam
jñātu kāmo mahātejā saha rāmaḥ kanīyasā |
verses.translation: On coming to the midstream of water there Rama heard an unusual and increasing noise of gushy waters along with his younger brother, and that brilliant one Rama desired to know its significance.

glosses.meaning: of water, in mid of stream, on coming

verses.devanagari:
अथ रामः सरिन्मध्ये पप्रच्छ मुनिपुङ्गवम्
वारिणो भिद्यमानस्य किमयं तुमुलो ध्वनिः |
verses.iast:
atha rāmaḥ sarin madhye papraccha muni puñgavam
vāriṇo bhidyamānasya kim ayam tumulo dhvaniḥ |
verses.translation: Rama then asked the eminent sage Vishvamitra in the midst of the river, "what is this turbulent sound sire, as though slashing water?"

verses.devanagari:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितम्
कथयामास धर्मात्मा तस्य शब्दस्य निश्चयम् |
verses.iast:
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā kautūhala samanvitam
kathayāmāsa dharmātmā tasya śabdasya niścayam |
verses.translation: On hearing the inquisitive words of Raghava that virtue-souled sage Vishvamitra started to tell the significance of that sound.

verses.devanagari:
कैलासपर्वते राम मनसा निर्मितं परम्
ब्रह्मणा नरशार्दूल तेनेदं मानसं सरः |
verses.iast:
kailāsa parvate rāma manasā nirmitam param
brahmaṇā naraśārdūla tena idam mānasam saraḥ |
verses.translation: "On Mt. Kailash Brahma created a great lake at his will, oh, tigerly-man Rama, hence that is called Maanasa Lake.

glosses.meaning: great, lake, at will, created - lake is the brainchild of Brahma

verses.devanagari:
तस्मात् सुस्राव सरसः सायोध्यामुपगूहते
सरः प्रवृत्ता सरयूः पुण्या ब्रह्मसरश्च्युता |
तस्यायमतुलः शब्दो जाह्नवीमभिवर्तते
वारिसंक्षोभजो राम प्रणामं नियतः कुरु |
verses.iast:
tasmāt susrāva sarasaḥ sā ayodhyām upagūhate
saraḥ pravṛttā sarayūḥ puṇyā brahma saraḥ cyutā |
tasya ayam atulaḥ śabdo jāhnavīm abhivartate
vāri saṅkṣobhajo rāma praṇāmam niyataḥ kuru |
verses.translation: "That river which spontaneously flows out of that Maanasa Lake surrounds Ayodhya city is this one, the River Sarayu. Because this has originated from a lake, saraH, this is known as Sarayu. And because it flows from Brahma's Lake it is a merited river. This is the remarkable noise of such a Sarayu River in its coursing towards River Ganga, generated by the collision of their waters, and Rama, offer regards to these rivers, respectfully." So said Vishvamitra to the princes.

glosses.meaning: [because] from sara [lake,] originated, [it is called] Sarayu river
to River Ganga, towards, coursing towards

verses.devanagari:
ताभ्यां तु तावुभौ कृत्वा प्रणाममतिधार्मिकौ
तीरं दक्षिणमासाद्य जग्मतुर्लघुविक्रमौ |
verses.iast:
tābhyām tu tāvubhau kṛtvā praṇāmam atidhārmikau
tīram dakṣiṇam āsādya jagmatur laghu vikramau |
verses.translation: Offering their salutations to River Sarayu and Ganga those two most virtuous and agile footed princes proceeded further on reaching the southern riverbank.

glosses.meaning: in swiftness, exerts, they proceeded further.

verses.devanagari:
स वनं घोरसंकाशं दृष्ट्वा नरवरात्मजः
अविप्रहतमैक्ष्वाकः पप्रच्छ मुनिपुंगवम् |
verses.iast:
sa vanam ghora saṅkāśam dṛṣṭvā naravarātmajaḥ
aviprahatam aikṣvākaḥ papraccha muni puṅgavam |
verses.translation: On seeing a horrendous and uninhibited forest, Rama, the son of the best king Dasharatha asked the eminent sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: [a vi pra hatam = not, verily, trodden] = untrodden - uninhibited

verses.devanagari:
अहो वनमिदं दुर्गं झिल्लिकागणसंयुतम्
भैरवैः श्वापदैः कीर्णं शकुनैर्दारुणारवैः |
verses.iast:
aho vanam idam durgam jhillikā gaṇa saṃyutam
bhairavaiḥ śvāpadaiḥ kīrṇam śakunaiḥ dāruṇa āravaiḥ |
verses.translation: "Oh, impenetrable is this forest fraught with swarms of crickets, brutish predators, and vultures, which are all horribly strident.

glosses.meaning: this, forest, difficult, to enter - impenetrable.

verses.devanagari:
नानाप्रकारैः शकुनैर्वाश्यद्भिर्भैरवस्वनैः
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहैश्च वारणैश्चापि शोभितम् |
verses.iast:
nānā prakāraiḥ śakunaiḥ vāśyadbhiḥ bhairava svanaiḥ
siṃha vyāghra varāhaiḥ ca vāraṇaiḥ ca api śobhitam |
verses.translation: "Various vultures are screeching with fierce sonority, and tigers, wild boars, and elephants render this forest atypical.

verses.devanagari:
धवाश्वकर्णककुभैर्बिल्वतिन्दुकपाटलैः
संकीर्णं बदरीभिश्च किंन्वेतद्दारुणं वनम् |
verses.iast:
dhava aśvakarṇa kakubhaiḥ bilva tinduka pāṭalaiḥ
saṅkīrṇam badarībhiḥ ca kim nu etat dāruṇam vanam |
verses.translation: "Indeed, what is this wretched forest that is dense with Dhava, Ashvakarna, Arjuna, Bilva, Tinduka, Patala, and Badari trees." Thus Rama asked Vishvamitra.
notes: The botanical names of the trees mentioned in the text are Grislea Tormentosa, Shorea Robusta, Echites Antidysenterica, Bignonia Suaveolens, Aegle Marmelos, and Diospyrus Glutinosa. I have omitted the Kutaja (Echites) and the Tinduka (Diospyrus). Griffith.

glosses.meaning: tree of Mimosa catechu family, Hindi: Khaira, khadira
trees of Diospyros glutinosa, Hindi: tamaala
with badarii trees of Zizyphus jujuba, also

verses.devanagari:
तमुवाच महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः
श्रूयतां वत्स काकुत्स्थ यस्यैतद्दारुणं वनम् |
verses.iast:
tam uvāca mahātejā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ
śrūyatām vatsa kākutstha yasya etat dāruṇam vanam |
verses.translation: The resplendent and the great saint Vishvamitra then said to Rama, "I will tell you, oh, my boy Rama, whose is this wretched forest.

glosses.meaning: I will let you hear - I will tell you, my boy
this one, wretched, forest, whose is.

verses.devanagari:
एतौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ पूर्वमास्तां नरौत्तम
मलदाश्च करूषाश्च देवनिर्माणनिर्मितौ |
verses.iast:
etau janapadau sphītau pūrvam āstām narauttama
maladāḥ ca karūṣāḥ ca deva nirmāṇa nirmitau |
verses.translation: "Once these were vast provinces, oh, best one among men, designed by gods and known as Malada and Karuusha.
notes: The word mala da is malam dyati khaṇḍayati iti mala da that which abolishes excreta, but not filth itself. karuśa is kā rūśa remover of hunger. If mortal hunger is there excreta will be there and then mortality of Indra is at stake. Hence if hunger is eliminated there will be nothing filthy. Once these provinces were such hunger removers equalling to heaven, but deteriorated in their heaven-on-earth attributes, owing to demoness Tataka.

glosses.meaning: oh, best one among men, Rama
of gods, by construction, that are constructed - designed by gods

verses.devanagari:
पुरा वृत्रवधे राम मलेन समभिप्लुतम्
क्षुधा चैव सहस्राक्षं ब्रह्महत्या समाविशत् |
verses.iast:
purā vṛtra vadhe rāma malena samabhiplutam
kṣudhā caiva sahasrākṣam brahma hatyā sam āviśat |
verses.translation: "Once upon a time, oh, Rama, mortal impurities of filth and hunger completely stained Indra when he eliminated demon Vritra, as he committed the sin of killing of a Brahman, where the demon Vritra was incidentally a Brahman.

verses.devanagari:
तमिन्द्रं मलिनं देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः
कलशैः स्नापयामासुर्मलं चास्य प्रमोचयन् |
verses.iast:
tam indram malinam devā ṛṣayaḥ ca tapodhanāḥ
kalaśaiḥ snāpayāmāsuḥ malam ca asya pramocayan |
verses.translation: "The gods and ascetically rich sages then started to bathe feculent Indra with their handy vessels for the riddance of his defilement.

verses.devanagari:
इह भूम्यां मलं दत्त्वा देवाः कारूषमेव च
शरीरजं महेन्द्रस्य ततो हर्षं प्रपेदिरे |
verses.iast:
iha bhūṃyām malam dattvā devāḥ kāruṣam eva ca
śarīrajam mahendrasya tato harṣam prapedire |
verses.translation: "On giving filth and hunger emerged out of the body of Mahendra here on the earth then the gods were gladdened.

verses.devanagari:
निर्मलो निष्करूषश्च शुचिरिन्द्रो यथाभवत्
ततो देशस्य सुप्रीतो वरं प्रादादनुत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
nirmalo niṣkarūṣaḥ ca śuddha indro yathā abhavat
tato deśasya suprīto varam prādād anuttamam |
verses.translation: "As and when Indra was without desecration and hunger as well, and thus purified, then gladdened about this place he gave it an unexcelled boon.

verses.devanagari:
इमौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ ख्यातिं लोके गमिष्यतः
मलदाश्च करूषाश्च ममांगमलधारिणौ |
verses.iast:
imau janapadau sphītau khyātim loke gamiṣyataḥ
maladāḥ ca karūṣāḥ ca mama aṅga mala dhāriṇau |
verses.translation: "These provinces that bear the impurity of my body shall become resourceful and they shall attain renown in world as Malada and Karusha." Thus Indra gave boon to this place.

glosses.meaning: these, habitats, will be resourceful places
in world, renown, they will attain.

verses.devanagari:
साधु साध्विति तं देवाः पाकशासनमब्रुवन्
देशस्य पूजां तां दृष्ट्वा कृतां शक्रेण धीमता |
verses.iast:
sādhu sādhu iti tam devāḥ pākaśāsanam abruvan
deśasya pūjām tām dṛṣṭvā kṛtām śakreṇa dhīmatā |
verses.translation: "On observing the honour accorded by wise Indra to these places gods praised the controller of demon Paaka, namely Indra saying, 'splendid, splendid it is.'

glosses.meaning: by wise one, Indra, done - according
demon Paaka, controller of - to Indra

verses.devanagari:
एतौ जनपदौ स्फीतौ दीर्घकालमरिन्दम
मलदाश्च करूषाश्च मुदितौ धनधान्यतः |
verses.iast:
etau janapadau sphītau dīrgha kālam arindama
maladāḥ ca karūṣāḥ ca muditā dhana dhānyataḥ |
verses.translation: "For a long time these habitations Malada and Karuusha were affluent, oh, enemy subjugator Rama, and people were happy with wealth and provisions.

verses.devanagari:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य यक्षी वै कामरूपिणी
बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्ती तदा ह्यभूत् |
ताटका नाम भद्रं ते भार्या सुन्दस्य धीमतः
मारीचो राक्षसः पुत्रो यस्याः शक्रपराक्रमः |
verses.iast:
kasya cit atha kālasya yakṣī kāma rūpiṇī
balam nāga sahasrasya dhārayantī tadā hi ābhūt |
tāṭakā nāma bhadram te bhāryā sundasya dhīmataḥ
mārīco rākṣasaḥ putro yasyāḥ śakra parākramaḥ |
verses.translation: "Later at sometime, a yaksha female who is a guise changer at her wish, possessor of the strength of a thousand elephants, wife of clever Sunanda, and she whose son is demon Mareecha, the one equal to Indra in his bravery, prevailed here, let you be safe Rama.

verses.devanagari:
वृत्तबाहुर्महाशीर्षो विपुलास्यतनुर्महान्
राक्षसो भैरवाकारो नित्यं त्रासयते प्रजाः |
verses.iast:
vṛtta bāhur mahā śīrṣo vipulā asya tanur mahān
rāxaso bhairava ākāro nityam trāsayate prajāḥ |
verses.translation: "That demon Mareecha is round shouldered, huge headed, cavernous mouthed, and gigantic bodied one, and he is always terrifying the people.

verses.devanagari:
इमौ जनपदौ नित्यं विनाशयति राघव
मलदांश्च करूषांश्च ताटका दुष्टचारिणी |
verses.iast:
imau janapadau nityam vināśayati rāghava
maladāṃśca karūṣāṃśca tāṭakā duṣṭa cāriṇī |
verses.translation: "And Raghava, that malevolent Tataka is always destroying the inhabitations at Malada and Karusha.

verses.devanagari:
सेयं पन्थानमावृत्य वसत्यध्यर्धयोजने
अतैव च गन्तव्यं ताटकाया वनं यतः |
verses.iast:
sā iyam panthānam āvṛtya vasati adhyardha yojane
ata eva ca gantavyam tāṭakāyā vanam yataḥ |
verses.translation: "She lives about one and half yojana distance from here, and by which reason this became the forest of Tataka, owing to her gruesome activities, for that reason only a headway is to be made, to eradicate her and her activities.
notes: This verse also means 'where there is the forest of Tataka there we have to go.' The above is another shade of that verse.

glosses.meaning: there alone / for that reason alone

verses.devanagari:
स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य जहीमां दुष्टचारिणीम्
मन्नियोगादिमं देशं कुरु निष्कण्टकं पुनः |
verses.iast:
sva bāhu balam āśritya jahi imām duṣṭa cāriṇīm
mat niyogāt imam deśam kuru niṣkaṇṭakam punaḥ |
verses.translation: "Depending upon the strength of your own self-confidence you have to eradicate this evildoer, and assigned by me you have to make this province free from thorniness.
notes: Great persons accomplish their deeds by their self-confidence, kriyā siddhiḥ sattve bhavati mahatām, na upakaraṇe not by their hardware.

glosses.meaning: your own, arms, strength - self-confidence, depending upon

verses.devanagari:
न हि कश्चिदिमं देशं शक्तो ह्यागन्तुमीदृशम्
यक्षिण्या घोरया राम उत्सादितमसह्यया |
verses.iast:
na hi kaścit imam deśam śakto hi āgantum īdṛśam
yakṣiṇyā ghorayā rāma utsāditam asahyayā |
verses.translation: "Indeed, none is able to enter this sort of province, Rama, destroyed by the hazardous and invincible unearthly being who turned into a demoness, namely Tataka, hence you have to make the provinces habitable.

glosses.meaning: destroyed, this kind of, to province

verses.devanagari:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथैतद्दारुणं वनम् |
यक्ष्या चोत्सादितं सर्वमद्यापि न निवर्तते
verses.iast:
etat te sarvam ākhyātam yathā etat dāruṇam vanam |
yakṣyā ca utsāditam sarvam adya api na nivartate
verses.translation: "As to how that ghoulish Tataka destroyed this entire forest, rendering it as a devastated place, without refraining from it even today, all that is narrated." So said Vishvamitra to Rama.

glosses.meaning: rendered it as a devastated one
not, returning - not retracing her steps - without refrain
that, all, to you, is narrated.
